findings.title: Nutrient associations need energy adjustment.
findings.detail: `kcal` is total energy. `protein`, `carb`, `fat_total`, `fat_sat`, `fat_mon` and `fat_poly` carry energy, and each correlates 0.72 to 0.88 with `kcal`.
findings.why_it_matters: People who eat more of everything eat more of anything, so every nutrient association is confounded by total intake; that adjustment is needed is not in dispute. Which method to use is a convention: the standard and residual methods estimate the same substitution, and the residual method's advantages are practical, not inferential.

decisions.sentence: The table was read through the `dietary` lens.
`glucose` was chosen as the outcome; it is measured on all `21,849` rows.
The analysis was declared for `prediction`: models are judged on rows they never saw.

Column roles were set for `28` columns: energy `kcal`; exposures `protein`, `sugar`, `carb` and 4 more; covariates `age`, `gender`, `bp_sys` and 9 more; identifier `SEQN`; flags `imputed_weight`, `imputed_height`, `imputed_bmi` and 3 more; time column `cycle_begin_year`.
`1,419` rows with `kcal` outside `500`–`3500` for `gender` `female` and outside `800`–`4200` for `male` were excluded as implausible intakes (Willett's sex-specific cut-offs).
Rows missing any predictor were dropped (a complete-case analysis): `2,864` of `20,430` rows remain.
A random `20%` of the `2,864` rows (seed `0`) was held out for one final score; models were compared by `5`-fold cross-validation on the rest.
Energy was adjusted by the residual method: `protein`, `carb`, `fat_total` and 3 more were each regressed on `kcal` on training rows and replaced by the residual plus the nutrient's mean.
Three model families were chosen: gradient-boosted trees, elastic net and linear regression.
